ranked_facts.why: The presence of linear C3 and IgG deposits along the basement membrane is more characteristic of Bullous Pemphigoid than Pemphigus Vulgaris or Dermatitis Herpetiformis, and this finding cannot be explained by Infectious Bullous Dermatosis or Other Bullous Dermatosis.

Tense axillary bullae are more typical of Bullous Pemphigoid, whereas Pemphigus Vulgaris often presents with flaccid bullae, and this distinction helps to differentiate between these two autoimmune bullous dermatoses.
